indexing.note: one flat-rate band from 0 (3.0% for 2025, IC 6-3-2-1), no threshold to grow
fixed by statute: 1,000 exemptions, 500 age-65 extra under a 40,000 AGI test (IC 6-3-1-3.5(a)(3)-(5))
fixed: 16,000 "for 2016 and thereafter" (IC 6-3-2-3.7, as stated in DOR Information Bulletin #6)

not_modelled.what: Civil service annuity deduction for a surviving spouse, who has no age requirement. A projection cannot tell a survivor annuity from the person's own annuity.
Disability retirement deduction of up to 5,200 per person, for someone permanently and totally disabled at retirement with Schedule IT-2440 signed by a doctor.
Exemptions for dependents (1,000 each), the additional exemption for certain dependent children (1,500, or 3,000 the first year) and the private school or homeschool deduction (1,000 per child).
1,000 exemption for a filer or spouse who is legally blind; a projection does not know this.

Renter's deduction (up to 3,000, or 1,500 married filing separately) and homeowner's property tax deduction (up to 2,500, or 1,250 married filing separately); a projection does not hold rent or Indiana property tax paid.
Deductions for active duty military pay and for National Guard and reserve pay; a projection cannot tell military pay from other wages.
Interest on direct U.S. government obligations is deducted (Schedule 2 line 4); a projection cannot tell it from other interest.

approximations.what: The surviving spouse branch of the civil service annuity deduction is not applied (not_modelled): a survivor under 62 gets no deduction.
The disability retirement deduction is not applied (not_modelled).
approximations.size: Up to 3% of 5,200 = 156 a year per person.

approximations.what: All municipal bond interest is treated as from other states and taxed; Indiana's own obligations are not added back, nor are other states' obligations held or acquired before Jan. 1, 2012.
Interest on U.S. government obligations is taxed (the projection cannot tell it from other interest).
Renter's and homeowner's deductions are not applied (not_modelled).
approximations.size: Up to 3% of 3,000 = 90 a year (renter) or 3% of 2,500 = 75 a year (homeowner).

approximations.what: Dependent exemptions and the private school deduction are not applied (not_modelled).
approximations.size: 30 a year per dependent, plus 45 (90 the first year) for a qualifying child.

approximations.what: The Unified Tax Credit for the Elderly, a refundable low-income credit outside the record's scope (record notes), is not applied.
approximations.size: At most 140 a year, and only with federal AGI under 10,000.

approximations.what: Indiana starts from federal AGI as of Jan. 1, 2023 (the Internal Revenue Code then in effect; Indiana does not currently follow P.L. 119-21); the projection uses the household's current federal AGI and applies no Schedule 1 add-backs other than municipal interest.
approximations.size: Usually none for retirement income; can matter for business items (bonus depreciation, section 179) the projection does not model.
